key_symbols.name: attachCmd (RunE)
key_symbols.role: reads the operator's own terminal size via term.GetSize(os.Stdout.Fd()) and hands it to AttachArgv before exec'ing tmux attach-session

key_symbols.name: Engine.AttachArgv
key_symbols.role: builds the attach argv, using the client-told cols/rows as the box for a chained select-layout, never a live query

key_symbols.name: chainedAttachArgv / bareAttachArgv
key_symbols.role: compose the tmux argv, chaining a client-sized select-layout onto attach-session via a literal ';' argv element

key_symbols.name: pinGeometryOptionsLocked
key_symbols.role: pins session/window-scoped 'status off' and 'window-size latest' before the told box can be trusted

key_symbols.name: readWindowSizeLatestLocked / readStatusRowsLocked
key_symbols.role: read back the EFFECTIVE option values (not trusting set-option's exit code) and reconcile them against what was pinned, suppressing the chain on mismatch

key_symbols.name: liveBoxLocked
key_symbols.role: queries the live tmux window size via display-message; falls back to cfg.Width/Height on error

key_symbols.name: planLayout
key_symbols.role: pure function mapping strand table + a told render.Box into a tmux window_layout string; never queries tmux itself

key_symbols.name: applyLayoutLocked
key_symbols.role: the live-query render path: gets liveBoxLocked's box and applies select-layout/select-pane

key_symbols.name: reconcileApplyPersistLocked
key_symbols.role: shared tail every strand-mutating op runs: reconcile dead panes -> re-list -> applyLayoutLocked (live box) -> persist state

key_symbols.name: errAttachChainSuppressed
key_symbols.role: sentinel marking a benign degrade-to-bare-attach when a told/live precondition fails

summary: Terminal geometry has two independent sources of truth that are never merged into one persisted value. On `lyx reed attach`, reedcli reads the operator's own pty size once via golang.org/x/term and passes it into Engine.AttachArgv as the 'told' box; AttachArgv pins 'status off' and 'window-size latest' on the session, then re-reads both options back (the explicit reconciliation point) and suppresses the chained select-layout if the readback disagrees with what was pinned, since only then is it guaranteed tmux will resize the window to the client's exact told size. When the chain is safe, the told box is planned into a window_layout string and chained onto attach-session with a literal ';' argv element, so it executes only after tmux has already resized the window to the attaching client -- landing verbatim rather than being rescaled. Every other strand-mutating operation (add/remove/resume, via reconcileApplyPersistLocked -> applyLayoutLocked) instead re-queries the session's live width/height fresh via a tmux display-message round trip (liveBoxLocked) and replans against that, falling back to the static cfg.Width/Height only on a query failure; there is no persisted last-known cols/rows in reed.json. Once a client is actually attached, ordinary window resizes (SIGWINCH) are handled entirely inside the tmux client process itself, which owns the operator's stdio after attach.Run() hands it off -- reed's Go code is not involved again until the next CLI invocation re-reads geometry.
